newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share index pauses from rising trend.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share index pauses from rising trend.

text.p: The Nigerian share index, enjoying a healthy growth since January, closed barely changed on Monday despite bullish moves on the stock exchange, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 7336.56 from 7336.57 on Thursday, the last day of trade.
"Investors continued to buy popular stocks, sending their prices higher still," one trader said. "But continued selling of conglomerate PZ shares held down the index."
The consumer goods giant plunged 10 kobo to 28.30 naira as investors flooded the market with large quantities of its shares following a recent bonus issue.
Northern Nigerian Flour Mills and Benue Cement also dropped by 10 kobo apiece because of lack of buyers. The miller closed at 8.90 naira and the cement firm at 6.50 naira.
Buyers pushed up FSB International Bank by nearly five percent, the maximum allowed in a day, to 7.10 naira.
Other big banks also soared. UBA rose 25 kobo to 8.00 naira while Union Bank was 20 kobo up at 8.80 naira.
West African Portland Cement Company, the leader in the sector added 10 kobo, closing at 55.30 naira. Dunlop was 8.70 naira and NCR was 10.30 naira, both 10 kobo higher.
Undiminished demand for oil marketers pushed Unipetrol and Total up 20 kobo, respectively to 68.40 naira and 66.20 naira.
